verdict.tagline: VR combat sandbox shines despite janky physics and simple enemies.
for_you_if: you want unmatched physics-based melee combat in virtual reality
you enjoy sandbox experimentation over structured campaigns
not_for_you_if: you experience severe motion sickness in virtual reality
you need stable frame rates during heavy visual effects
you lack patience for simplistic enemy artificial intelligence

distortion_flags.sentence: Negative sentiment drops sharply past the opening hours before stabilizing at high recommendation rates.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering severe motion sickness and nausea while playing.

citations.review_text: its okay but it causes severe motion sickness.

Really rather disappointed with this. After having to troubleshoot the fact that the game didn't respond to my controllers at all, found I had to, for whatever inane reason, hit spacebar twice to get it to pick up... literally anything other than head movements. Thought, okay, that's weird, but nothing unforgivable.

Create a character, go into the game, and suddenly my head movements are tracking in the opposite direction. If I turn my head left physically, my camera turns like my character is looking right. Absolutely debilitating and almost instant nausea over this. It was fine while I was in menus, and now it's backwards for seemingly no explainable reason. Try to get back to the main menu before the urge to vomit overtakes me, thinking maybe there's a setting I can adjust, but nothing I seem to press will bring up anything resembling a menu.

Try to navigate through the tutorial with as little movement as possible, and it's telling me to use my right thumbpad to turn. Except it will only turn in one direction: Left. Pressing the right one does nothing. Don't know why. Find out with a google search that this is apparently bound to some menu I presumably don't have access to. So I can only turn left, then? 

I'm sad to say I gave up on this. Between the constant issues at the start and what just seems like a disaster class in controller mapping, I did not consider this worth it. Grateful I managed to at least get a refund.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that melee combat physics feel janky, and enemies can be exploited because they cannot attack when grabbed or knocked to the ground.

citations.review_text: The melee AI sucks really badly, making the game pitifully easy. I mean once they're on the ground, or even if you grab their shoulder, the enemy literally cannot attack.
The magic system is alright but overall combat physics are janky and clunky. Enemies are repetitive and crystal hunt mode is boring and uninspired.

I wouldn't tell people not to buy this game. There's probably a lot of fun to be had. But it definitely didn't feel at the level the reviews I read suggested.

There is a good amount of jank and for the price I couldn't help but feel like I was playing modded Skyrim VR. Some mechanics like the journal and the zipwire pulley should have had a quick store option instead of manually putting them into your inventory. Some of the physics feel weird, like your blade getting knocked around by impacting enemy-held items and not seeming to have the weight of their weapons. Although the game tells you you can, using other physics items like blades held in both hands to slide on ziplines did not work for me and sent me tumbling. 

Weapons looted from enemies are "stolen," so you cannot keep them after dungeons. I find it odd that you are going to a dungeon for the purpose of finding loot, encountering enemies that try to kill you on sight, and the game draws the line at keeping the weapons that you can take and use to kill their owners. 

Spells seem to need to be set with every change in environment and do not stay equipped. Initial spells seem to be useless, I couldn't tell if the base fireball actually staggered enemies or not and flailing with a short blade seemed far more effective to get them off-balance, which they return to unnaturally quickly. 

The initial dungeons feel cookie-cutter and when going to the second dungeon, I wasn't sure for awhile if I hadn't selected the first again by mistake. Dungeons are mostly devoid of loot until the chest at the end. There is loot mixed in, just enough to have you checking dead ends and empty corners that turn up dry.

Definitely worth a try to see if it's your thing, but it feels to me at least to be 5 years older than it is when playing it.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Longer-term players highlight unintelligent enemy artificial intelligence and mod compatibility hurdles after updates.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that enemy AI is unintelligent and predictable, though some point out that mods or older versions can alter the challenge.

citations.review_text: Fun with mods. I wish the AI was more like U6 or 7 because I feel they were more challenging that way.

something I realize about this game is that the newer the version is, the more mods I need to make the game better. no matter what, I can't get myself to keep playing the latest version of the game because of how stupid the AI is. for new players, please try out version U12 or below if the AI is too stupid for you.

satisfying combat, lotta weapons, spells have good interaction with the world (though they are incredibly overpowered at times, especially later game)
enemies do feel a tad rigid and move around faster than would really make sense irl, and you're a bit slow when you aren't swinging your arms to run (which you can't do while strafing but enemies can)
the enemy ai is really stupid and uncoordinated too, but that's par for the course in these kinds of games honestly. the only real threat is later on when [spoiler]sorcerers gain a hitscan crossmap electric beam that deals a quarter of your health[/spoiler] or when you're trying to melee the [spoiler]rock titan[/spoiler] boss thing
it's very loosely physics based tbh, nowhere near the same extent of physics as boneworks or half sword, but it doesn't take you out of it much
the gore's pretty good and it's satisfying to behead enemies after you've knocked them down
plate armor interaction when worn by you is completely unrealistic, but if it was it would be pretty much impossible to die so it makes sense why they'd do it this way
the dungeon runs are really fun and it's a satisfying gameplay loop, you can play for hours and not get bored (at least until you get a headache)
you aren't able to keep enemies' weapons after you leave the level you're in (it gets labeled as "stolen" when you have it which prevents you from keeping it), which is obviously unrealistic when the game's fine with you stealing all of the riches and healing items and trinkets, but it would break the main gameplay loop if you could just take everything you wanted so it's fair
the baron's kinda fun to listen to, his voice is nice and he's somewhat sociable as a character (not that you can actually talk to him or anything, but his character is nice. i think he might be the only actual named character you see in the game, so that's something)

claims.claim: Reviewers note that game updates cause mod incompatibility issues that require waiting for creators to update files.

citations.review_text:
Blade & Sorcery is the ultimate VR combat experience. Even in its vanilla state, the game shines with its highly interactive gameplay and immersive progression. However, the true magic lies in its incredible modding community. Thanks to the convenient built-in mod manager, you can easily transform into your favorite anime characters or add custom weapons with just a few clicks. The only downside is that the game's consistent updates frequently cause mod incompatibility issues, requiring you to wait for creators to update their files. Despite this minor annoyance, it is an absolute must-play masterpiece.

(AI was used to regrammarize this review)
This may be the highest quality VR game out there and for me it is the most fun VR game i have ever played. Every update makes the game more complex and fun. Fully recommend. 10/10

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Veterans point out visual duplication in dungeons, predictable opponents, and bugs introduced by patches.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the dungeon exploration as suffering from visual repetition due to copying and pasting the same rooms.

citations.review_text: An insanely fun and brutal physics based VR game. This review is primarily from my Crystal Hunt play-through but also experience in sandbox. The game has a pretty wise variety of weapons that feel very good to use. The weapons plus the very fun to use magic open up a good bit of play-styles to choose from. The cool particle effects & various abilities of the game's magic make combat super satisfying and open up creative ways to defeat enemies. The Crystal Hunt mode is enjoyable, but I think with the new updates adding factions that have a largely different style, there should be dungeons with a different visual style. There is only the normal dungeons and the one Dalgarian dungeon per progression stage; I feel like there's a lot of visual repetition at a certain point. Overall, this is a very fun VR game to release some energy and just have fun simple, brutal fun.

The base game.. Lacks.. its really cool at first but NPC's well act like you'd imagine old internet NPC's act they freeze hesitate to attack and barely present a threat. the story is rather great and interesting as you are invited to explore highly detailed dungeons even if its the same two dozen rooms copy and pasted.
the physics are great tho a bit busted in damage, hell you can make basically anything work.

Now in terms of modding for example i do HEMA so i use adaptive AI which fix's the AI and Makes them a actual threat i love it tho most things can be cherry pciekd with mods

Base game 7.3/10
Mods 10/10
The modding space is so big with near endless possiblitys

claims.claim: Reviewers state that enemy artificial intelligence is limited, describing opponents as dumb, prone to freezing, hesitant to attack, or easily predictable.

citations.review_text:
I have been playing since U5 and I can safely say: I absolutely adore the game!

The controls are nice, mechanics are pleasant and Crystal Hunt is a very fun addition too. Enemies can be a bit dumb, but that only adds to the fun.

The weapons feel nice to swing, especially requiring two hand for weapons that would require it in real life too.

The imbueing system is super fun and the customizability with the spells and thus imbues is just the icing on the cake.

The fact that this is also fully playable WITHOUT weapons is even more fun.

This game is also highly moddable, even in game, which makes it so much better, so that we don't HAVE to struggle with websites like Nexusmods and it's mod installer.

Keep it up devs, I love the work you guys have done so far and I am beyond excited for future updates!

Has freedom that most VR games don't have. Not the best combat AI, but you do have a  more control over what you can do with them. You can also get a little bit creative, trying out new techniques or tricks that most VR games simply can't allow you to do.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that game updates introduce bugs that affect enemy behavior and combat mechanics, such as enemies spasming or disappearing, weapons phasing through opponents, and hands getting stuck mid-swing.

citations.review_text:
I really like and will always support this game but the quaility control on these updates are extremely lacking, every update introduces a new bug that seemingly never gets fixed, I've played since U9 and remember pretty well that before 1.0 I never saw these bugs.

 In the current version with no mods it feels like at least 1/4 NPCs that I try to fight will always bug out, whether it be them spasing out and disappearing, my weapons phasing through them or my hand getting stuck in place mid swing, I can never get through a squad of enemies without it glitching out, this game just feels really clunky and bad to play right now, don't get me wrong, this game has always been janky but it feels like we are going backwards in quailty, I love all the new content but every update has me playing less and less.

i REALLY Wat to like this game but every update is all the same
new medeling content layered overtop a game that is still suffering from early access syndrome

each new update has in no way adressed the ever growing buggy gameplay at the core
the enemies are more wobbly than ever more unwilling to attack than ever and more likely to only attack my back than ever all while enemy attacks will still clip through my shield and count as a hit 

an performance hasnt been improved in the slightest all i can even say is they allowed us to make the game look worse than it already is to get better performance
